A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical visual recognition study despite retitling and reformatting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, visual and textual probing experiments, prompt ablations, and LoRA finetuning results, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional model comparisons, HierarCaps results, few-shot evaluations, and a hierarchy-free text-probing control.

M1.justification: The SigLIP-based distractor construction, visual/text probing approach, and visual/text-only LoRA procedures are retained. The additional prompting variants are diagnostic controls rather than changes to the proposed model or training method.

E1.justification: v2 adds HierarCaps evaluation in Appendix B.8 and Table 12, extending coverage from category taxonomies to hierarchies of abstract and detailed scene captions. This introduces a distinct semantic recognition setting. The original biological, ImageNet, food, and general-VQA evaluations remain.

E2.justification: The principal comparisons expand from six to ten open-source VLLMs and from two to four CLIP models. v2 actually evaluates LLaVA-OV-1.5-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B/32B, Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B, BioCLIP, and BioCLIP2 alongside the retained models, substantially broadening both contemporary and domain-specialized comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 0–5-shot sweep, a leaf-label-only probing input, and full-hierarchy versus last-two-level HCA on HierarCaps. Existing probing and LoRA splits and budgets remain unchanged. The reported ImgNet-Artifact depth changes from eight to seven while its level distribution stays identical, indicating a reporting correction rather than established rerunning. The few-shot experiment's input modality is not fully clarified.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing whether few-shot examples remedy poor consistency and whether text embeddings retain hierarchy without a hierarchy-specific question (Prompt 4, Figure 5). The HierarCaps analysis additionally excludes ambiguous upper levels. These extend the existing diagnostic suite; earlier prompt, depth, probing, and finetuning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The Pearson-correlation analysis and its reported coefficients are retained.

E6.justification: New model rows, HierarCaps scores, few-shot results, and the Prompt 4 curve substantially expand the reported evidence. For example, BioCLIP2 achieves 37.91 HCA and 95.26 leaf accuracy on iNat21-Plant; Qwen2.5-VL-7B achieves 7.10 and 77.10 on HierarCaps. Table 8 corrects swapped HCA/leaf entries for Qwen2.5-VL-32B and 72B; the 32B HCA changes from 46.98 to 26.90, matching the unchanged main-table result. Existing LoRA results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The hierarchy formulation, HCA and leaf-accuracy definitions, POR/S-POR/TOR formulas, and associated mathematical reasoning are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly restricts the title and abstract's bottleneck framing to open-source models, bringing forward a qualification already present in v1's body. It also adds the opening assertion that LLMs can hinder computer-vision research. The central consistency, probing, and finetuning claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving BioCLIP specialization, ambiguous HierarCaps captions, and dataset differences in hierarchy depth, abstract labels, and multiple objects. Its GPT-4o discussion softens 'the LLM part is not' the bottleneck to a conjecture that it is likely not. The existing limitations are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 documents taxonomy verification and removal of ambiguous or inconsistent nodes, expanding v1's brief refinement description without establishing that the underlying datasets changed. v2 also supplies checkpoint identifiers for the added models and new prompt examples. Existing optimization, hardware, training-time, and project-access information remains.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of language-model taxonomy knowledge through IS-A prediction, transitivity, ONTOLAMA, and TaxoLLaMA, and adds references supporting the new models, HierarCaps, and pretraining interpretation. These are targeted extensions; the central positioning relative to hierarchical CLIP and fine-grained VLLM research remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, opening argument, terminology, and several headings are revised. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, and the appendix discussion sections are reordered. Much of the technical exposition and experimental narrative is retained, so the rewriting is limited despite the extensive reformatting.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from single-column to two-column layout, with resized and relocated displays and a new opening callout. The dataset overview moves to the appendix, comparison tables expand, and HierarCaps and few-shot tables are added. Figure 5 adds Prompt 4, corrects the probing axis to 'Layer Index,' and substitutes an InternVL comparison already available in Figure 12.

improvement.justification: Direct BioCLIP comparisons, the caption-hierarchy evaluation, and the hierarchy-free probe strengthen the breadth and support for the retained diagnosis. Taxonomy-curation details and more cautious GPT-4o interpretation also help. The gains remain incremental, and some descriptions lag the additions: Appendix B.7 still calls LLaVA-OV-7B the strongest 7B/8B Food-101 model, although Table 11 gives Qwen3-VL-8B higher HCA, 51.76 versus 46.45.
